prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a bedroom layout across the five frames as the camera wearer turns from facing a bed with stacked pillows on the right and a window on the left (frames 1-2), tilts upward toward three framed wall pictures above the bed (frame 3), turns past a bedside lamp on the right (frame 4), and finally faces a wide rear window with a standing person on the far left and a lamp on the lower right (frame 5). In frames 1 to 3, the pillows and right-hand wall are bright white and within arm's reach at roughly 0.5 to 1.2 metres, while the bedside lamp sits about 1.5 to 2 metres away beside the bed and the window wall is roughly 2.5 to 3.5 metres away. In frame 5, the standing person on the left is rendered as a medium-grey silhouette about 2 to 2.5 metres in front of the camera wearer and roughly 0.5 metres in front of the darker rear window (~3 metres away), while a second lamp on the far lower right is closer at about 1.5 metres and about 2.5 metres to the right of the person. The depth map clearly separates the backlit person's silhouette from the bright window behind them and captures the continuous receding plane of the right-hand wall, which is hard to judge in the motion-blurred and overexposed RGB frames. However, the map is unreliable in frame 4 where the glowing lampshade and upper wall are assigned overly dark (far) values compared to frame 3, and on the glass window panes where outdoor trees and indoor reflections produce inconsistent depth estimates.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is entirely blank in frames 1, 2, and 4, detects only a single green mask mislabelled as a 'microwave' in the centre of frame 3, and identifies a pink 'person' mask on the far left of frame 5. Using the RGB strip for context, the frame 3 mask actually corresponds to the middle framed picture hanging on the right wall about 1 to 1.5 metres away (just above the bed pillows and between two other framed pictures that go undetected), while the frame 5 mask captures the standing person about 2 to 2.5 metres away in front of the left side of the window. The person's mask shows their head and torso facing roughly toward the camera wearer and slightly to the right, with their lower body cropped out of view by the bottom frame edge and their left side slightly overlapping the window frame behind them. In frame 5, the segmentation mask provides a cleaner boundary of the dark, backlit person against the high-contrast window than the shadowy RGB image alone. However, the map is largely unreliable across the sequence because it misses the bed, pillows, lamps, windows, and outer wall frames entirely, and falsely classifies the middle wall artwork in frame 3 as a microwave.
descriptions.pose: The pose map contains no detections in frames 1 through 4 as the camera wearer rotates around the empty bed and wall area, and displays a single yellow body skeleton on the left side of frame 5 where the standing person enters the field of view. In frame 5, the skeleton places the person about 2 to 2.5 metres in front of the camera wearer and to the left of the wide window, with facial keypoints clustered near the top indicating the head is turned toward the camera wearer. Only the left shoulder, left elbow, left wrist, and left hip joints are rendered, showing the person's left arm hanging down behind their back within arm's reach of the window sill behind them, while the right arm and lower legs are completely absent or occluded in shadow and cropped at the bottom of the frame. This skeletal overlay makes the exact joint locations of the person's left arm and hip visible despite the severe backlighting and dark clothing that obscure their torso in the RGB frame. The pose map is unreliable in omitting the person's right shoulder and right arm (which are dimly visible on the far left edge of the RGB frame) and detects no magenta hand keypoints at all.
